- Model consistently underestimates true prices, especially in the early part of the 30-day window.
- Forecasts show a gradual upward trend, but true outcomes often dip sharply after initial spikes or show mean-reversion to lower levels.
- Overshoots occur after sharp price spikes in history; model overreacts and continues upward beyond true mean.
- Model fails to capture sudden downward corrections or volatility spikes in the latter half of the forecast horizon.
- Forecasts tend to be smoother than actual price movements, missing short-term volatility and sharp reversals.
- Model exhibits persistent bias toward higher values, particularly when history includes recent high prices.
- True outcomes often show a “rebound” or “reset” after a low, while model continues upward trend.
- Model underestimates the magnitude of corrections following spikes, especially in the 20–30 day horizon.
- Forecasts are overly optimistic in the first 5–10 days, then gradually flatten — while true prices often show a more aggressive correction or rebound later.
